criteria.label: A
criteria.description: Non-accidental act or acts (excluding physical and sexual abuse acts) or threat adversely affecting the psychological well-being of the partner, such as those listed below. Acts not listed, but of similar severity are also eligible.

elements.description: Berating, disparaging, degrading, humiliating victim (or other similar behavior)
Restricting victim's ability to come and go freely (when unwarranted)
Obstructing victim's access to assistance (including, but not limited to, law enforcement, legal protective or medical resources, including FAP, a victim advocate, military command, or DV shelter)
Threatening victim (including, but not limited to, indicating/implying future physical harm, sexual assault, threats to kill)
Harming, or indicating that abuser will harm, people/things that victim cares about, such as children, self, other people, pets or property
Restricting victim's access to or use of economic resources (when unwarranted)
Restricting victim's access to or use of military services (including, but not limited to, taking away Family member's ID)
Isolating victim from family, friends, or social support resources
Trying to make victim think that s/he is crazy (or make others think that victim is mentally ill)

criteria.label: B
criteria.description: Significant impact on the partner involving any of the following:

elements.label: B. 1
elements.description: Psychological harm including any of the following:

sub_elements.label: a
sub_elements.description: Victim's more than inconsequential fear reaction (see footnote)

sub_elements.label: b
sub_elements.description: Significant psychological distress (Major Depressive Disorder, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, Acute Stress Disorder, or other psychiatric disorders, at or near diagnostic thresholds) related to, or exacerbated by, the act(s).

sub_elements.label: c
sub_elements.description: Victim's fear of emotionally abusive act(s) that significantly interfere(s) with the victim's ability to carry out any of these five major life activities: work; education; religion; necessary medical or mental health services; or contact with family/friends.

elements.label: B. 2
elements.description: Stress-related somatic symptoms (related to or exacerbated by the acts) that significantly interfere with normal functioning.

footnotes.label: More than inconsequential fear reaction
footnotes.definition: is defined as: (a) Fear (verbalized or displayed) of bodily injury to self or others AND (b) At least one of the following signs of fear or anxiety lasting at least 48 hours:
footnotes.required_component_a: Fear (verbalized or displayed) of bodily injury to self or others

required_component_b.description: Persistent intrusive recollections of the incident.

Marked negative reactions to cues related to incident, as evidenced by: (a) avoidance of cues; (b) subjective or overt distress to cues; or (c) physiological hyper-arousal to cues. (NOTE: Abuser can be a cue).
Acting or feeling as if incident is recurring.
Marked symptoms of anxiety (any of the following):
sub_elements: Hyper-vigilance (i.e., acting overly sensitive to sounds and sights in the environment; scanning the environment expecting danger; feeling keyed up and on edge).

rows.label: B. 1c
rows.short_description: Fear interferes with employment; education; religious faith; necessary medical or mental health service; or contact with family/friends

overall_decision.label: Overall Substantiation Finding
overall_decision.description: Did this case end up meeting all criteria for the type of maltreatment?
